newsitem.title: USA: Mysterious Illinois courtroom bombing injures judge.
newsitem.headline: Mysterious Illinois courtroom bombing injures judge.

text.p: A judge presiding over a civil trial escaped death on Tuesday by diving under his desk when a man suddenly appeared in the courtroom and tossed a Molotov cocktail at him.
Police said they had no suspects but were exploring revenge as a possible motive.
The wood-panelled, carpeted courtroom of Judge George Miller at the Champaign County Courthouse was ravaged by the ensuing fire that nearly reduced the chair in which he was sitting to ashes.

Miller, 69, gashed his forehead when he dove under his desk as the firebomb bounced off him. He was able to walk to an ambulance and was treated at a hospital where several stitches were required to close his wound.

The intense fire that followed was put out in about 20 minutes and officials said the 96-year-old, three-story courthouse suffered no structural damage. Damage to the courtroom was estimated at $100,000.
Two people were detained for questioning by police but later released.

One juror injured her knee in the stampede that followed the incident and several people were treated at the scene for cuts, possibly from flying glass from the smashed bottle, which did not explode, but leaked flammable fluid.
Defence lawyer Rich Harden said he was listening to a witness testify when he heard someone muttering and turned toward the back of the third-floor courtroom.
"I saw a man with a hood. He had a bottle with something sticking out. It had a very powerful smell and it looked like he had a lighter," Harden said. "I got out of the courtroom by a side door."
The opposing attorney in the medical malpractice case, Bob Kirchner, said he pursued the attacker who fled after throwing the bottle at the judge.
"As soon as he threw it he ran out of the courtroom. I ran after him," Kirchner said.
Authorities said it was the first such attack at the courthouse, which does not have particularly tight security or metal detectors.

Last year, an after-hours bombing of the prosecutor's office at the courthouse in adjacent Douglas County prompted increased security there, and the issue had become a minor controversy at the Champaign County Courthouse in Urbana.
Urbana and neighbouring Champaign, is home to the University of Illinois, about 100 miles (161 km) south of Chicago.
